method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan' (published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019)). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11097703). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Uveitis accounts for roughly 10% of visual impairment in developed countries,** and its complications (cataract, glaucoma, macular oedema) make prompt treatment essential.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Corticosteroids are the foundation of treatment for non-infectious uveitis,** and can be given as drops, by local injection or systemically.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No steroid drops if the cornea is infected** — herpes simplex, bacterial or fungal keratitis — because local immune suppression can make a sight-threatening infection worse.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Systemic steroids are contraindicated in active bacterial, fungal or viral infection, including TB,** since they can reactivate latent TB. Tuberculous uveitis may still get oral steroid once effective anti-TB treatment has begun.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before systemic steroids, take a full history** (osteoporosis, uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension, peptic ulcer, heart failure, hypersensitivity) **and screen for latent infection such as TB and syphilis.**
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Drops are the standard for anterior-segment inflammation;** anterior uveitis is the commonest form and is usually treated this way.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most drops barely reach the back of the eye,** so intermediate, posterior and panuveitis need another route.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe anterior inflammation (anterior-chamber cells 3+ or more): a potent steroid such as prednisolone acetate 1%, as often as one drop hourly at first,** then a gradual taper.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start tapering once anterior-chamber cells improve.** SUN defines improvement as a fall of two grades (for example 3+ to 1+) or to inactive (trace to 0). Aim for no inflammation, or minimal inflammation without relapse, on the fewest drops.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For chronic anterior uveitis, a gentler maintenance drop is advised:** fluorometholone 0.1%, one drop twice a day.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid steroid drops in known steroid responders or primary open-angle glaucoma,** and with corneal thinning or perforation; long use raises IOP and can cause irreversible optic-nerve damage.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider local injection** to add to systemic treatment or replace it when contraindicated, when adherence to drops or tablets is poor, and for severe one-sided uveitis or cystoid macular oedema that has not responded.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Match the route to the time needed:** for control under 3 months, periocular or intravitreal betamethasone, dexamethasone or triamcinolone; for control beyond 3 months, an intravitreal steroid implant.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For uveitic macular oedema, intravitreal treatment may be the better first choice:** in the POINT trial, intravitreal triamcinolone and the dexamethasone implant both beat periocular triamcinolone, at the cost of slightly more mild IOP rises.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Implants carry intraocular risks — cataract, glaucoma and infection — so monitor for them.** The longer-acting fluocinolone implant (Retisert) causes more steroid complications.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Use systemic steroids when sight is threatened** (retinal vasculitis, retinal detachment, choroidal neovascularisation, corrected acuity 6/60 or worse, or no view of the fundus), **when local therapy fails, or for bilateral or systemic disease** such as sarcoidosis, Behçet disease or Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral prednisone is the usual first choice, starting at 0.5 to 1 mg/kg/day by severity,** then tapered to response.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In severe uveitis, consider IV methylprednisolone pulses of 500–1000 mg a day for three days,** followed by a gradually reducing oral dose.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Taper in ever-smaller steps to limit relapse.** For long-term use, 7.5 mg a day is regarded as the safer maintenance dose.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If a safe maintenance steroid dose cannot be reached, add an immunosuppressant or a biologic.** Methotrexate, azathioprine or mycophenolate spare steroid; TNF inhibitors come in when conventional agents fail or are not tolerated.
claims.locator: Chang YC, Kao TE et al. (Taiwan Ocular Inflammation Society panel), Annals of Medicine, 'Use of corticosteroids in non-infectious uveitis: expert consensus in Taiwan', published 15 May 2024 (doi 10.1080/07853890.2024.2352019), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11097703/, retrieved 2026-09-23
